## About the group:

We are ecologists with a range of interests mainly related to the migration and foraging ecology of vertebrates (particularly birds) and the application of stable isotope techniques in ecology. Our research focuses on spatial and trophic ecology of animals, with a particular interest in the causes and consequences of intra-population variation in movement and foraging behaviours. Our main study systems is the population of Light-bellied Brent Geese that breed in the Canadian Arctic. We study this population across the annual cycle including Ireland, Iceland and Canada and we are currently using this system to understand the causes and consequences of migration-related body transformations.
